# Clubs

Thirty clubs for the 2026 season, fifteen per conference. 2026 is the first MLS season in over twenty years with no expansion club added or planned; San Diego FC (2025) remains the most recent addition.

> **No MLS club publishes a public brand-guidelines PDF with hex values. Every value here is second-hand unless marked high. Print and merchandise work must be verified against each club's own brand team.**
>
> Every value carries a confidence rating. Where sources disagree materially the value is marked **Low**; where no trustworthy value exists it is `null` rather than a guess. Full per-club disagreements are listed at the bottom of this page and in `data/clubs.json`.
>
> Where a Pantone-derived value and a web-derived value differ, this file carries the web value. For print, request the club's Pantone build.

## Confidence key

| Rating | Meaning |
|---|---|
| High | Corroborated by the club's own site or launch release plus at least one independent source. |
| Medium | Multiple third-party sources agree, no direct club-published hex found. |
| **Low** | Sources disagree materially, or a single crowd-sourced value only. Verify before print or licensed use. |
| **Unverified** | No trustworthy hex found. Value is null. Do not substitute a guess. |

## Theming

```html
<div data-club="por">…</div>
```

Sets `--mls-club-primary` / `-secondary` / `-tertiary` (true brand values, never altered) and `--mls-color-accent-*` (contrast-corrected for UI). See [03 Colour](03-color.md).

## Contrast-corrected accents

24 of 30 club primaries fail contrast on at least one background and are corrected in OKLab, adjusting lightness only so hue and chroma survive. **`--mls-club-primary` always holds the true, uncorrected value.**

Where a primary is achromatic — LAFC and D.C. United are both black — the accent is promoted to a chromatic club colour instead, because lightening black gives grey, and grey is the absence of a brand colour rather than one.

## Naming

See [09 Vocabulary](09-vocabulary.md) for suffix placement, second-reference forms, and the plural-verb rule. There is no pattern for suffix placement — it is a lookup table, and `data/clubs.json` is that table.

## Per-club notes and disagreements

**Atlanta United FC** — Four competing reds in circulation. #80000A is a clear outlier and should be discarded. Black is likely Pantone Black C.

**Charlotte FC** — MLS's launch release names four colours including silver, but no source publishes a silver hex. Left null deliberately.

**Chicago Fire FC** — Print build of Fire Red is #D50032 (Pantone-derived). #FF0000 is the web value.

**Colorado Rapids** — Crest redesign announced April 2026, no launch date. Club confirmed burgundy and light blue are retained, so this palette stands.

**Columbus Crew** — Dropped the 'SC' suffix in 2021. Pre-2021 material correctly reads 'Columbus Crew SC'.

**D.C. United** — Three-way split on the red: #EF3E42 (club site), #E4002B (Pantone-derived), #D61018 (ESPN). Club site value used. Takes periods, unlike LA Galaxy.

**FC Dallas** — Colour names are style-guide-derived and trustworthy; the hex builds are not.

**Houston Dynamo FC** — Official name of the orange is disputed between sources ('Wildcatter Orange' vs 'Electric Orange'). Hex is solid.

**Inter Miami CF** — CF trails the name. Contrast with CF Montreal, where CF leads.

**LA Galaxy** — Five competing golds. Club appears to carry both a Gold and a Dark Gold. No periods in 'LA' -- contrast with D.C. United. Only club with a gold five-title star.

**Los Angeles Football Club** — Six near-identical golds in circulation. 'Glory Red' appears on a single crowd source only. Never 'LA FC' with a space.

**Minnesota United FC** — No two sources agree on any of the three values. Verify before use.

**CF Montréal** — The e-acute is mandatory in all published copy. Use nameLocalised. CF leads the name. French-first club; Quebec French uses 'soccer', not 'football'.

**New England Revolution** — Print build of the red is #C8102E.

**New York City FC** — 2025 brand refresh. Pre-2025 values (#6CACE4 / #041E42 / #F15524) are obsolete -- do not inherit them from older references.

**New York Red Bulls** — Worst-documented palette in the league: four reds and two yellows across four sources. 'Red Bull New York' is the corporate entity name; 'New York Red Bulls' is the team name used in editorial, standings and headlines. MLS's own style guide lists the tricode as NY; asset filenames and ESPN use RBNY.

**Portland Timbers** — The 2013 Timbers Army tifo is credited in press coverage as the inspiration for the three stars on the league crest.

**Real Salt Lake** — The bright #F1CB00 gold circulating in older references looks pre-rebrand. Use #DAAA00.

**San Diego FC** — The club has publicly named its colours Chrome and Azul but has never published hex values. Azul candidates span #051222 to #06172B. Chrome is defined by the club as reflective -- it arguably has no single hue. The community palette is a gradient, not a fixed value. This club MUST be verified directly before any use.

**Seattle Sounders FC** — 2024 brand evolution retuned Rave Green and Pacific Blue and added Heritage Aqua. The pre-2024 green #5D9741 is obsolete.

**Sporting Kansas City** — Never 'Kansas City Sporting'. 'Sporting KC' is second reference only.

**St. Louis CITY SC** — CITY is all caps -- confirmed on the club's own site. MLS's scores page renders 'St. Louis City SC', which contradicts the club's own branding; follow the club. Club officially names four colours but publishes no hex values for the last two. Reserve side is CITY2.

**Toronto FC** — Unresolved three-way split on the red: #A6192E (PMS 187), #AA182C (ESPN), #B81137 (club site). One source cites Pantone 200 C, which converts to none of them.
